<h1 style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:right;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:normal;">Exhibit 31.1</font></h1>

<p align=center style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:115%;">CERTIFICATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:115%;">I, Ryan M. Lance, certify that:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">1.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">I have reviewed this quarterly report
on Form 10-Q of ConocoPhillips;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">2.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Based on my knowledge, this report
does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a
material fact necessary to make the statements made, in light of the
circumstances under which such statements were made, not misleading with respect
to the period covered by this report;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">3.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Based on my knowledge, the
financial statements, and other financial information included in this report,
fairly present in all material respects the financial condition, results of
operations and cash flows of the registrant as of, and for, the periods
presented in this report;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">4.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">The registrant&#8217;s other certifying
officer and I are responsible for establishing and maintaining disclosure
controls and procedures (as defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e))
and internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Exchange Act Rules
13a&#8209;15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:99.0pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(a)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Designed such disclosure controls
and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be
designed under our supervision, to ensure that material information relating to
the registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to us by
others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this
report is being prepared;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(b)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Designed such internal control
over financial reporting, or caused such internal control over financial
reporting to be designed under our supervision, to provide reasonable assurance
regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial
statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted
accounting principles;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(c)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Evaluated the effectiveness of the
registrant&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures and presented in this report
our conclusions about the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and
procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this report based on such
evaluation; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(d)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Disclosed in this report any
change in the registrant&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting that
occurred during the registrant&#8217;s most recent fiscal quarter (the registrant&#8217;s
fourth fiscal quarter in the case of an annual report) that has materially
affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the registrant&#8217;s
internal control over financial reporting; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">5.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">The registrant&#8217;s other certifying
officer and I have disclosed, based on our most recent evaluation of internal
control over financial reporting, to the registrant&#8217;s auditors and the audit
committee of the registrant&#8217;s board of directors (or persons performing the
equivalent functions):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(a)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">All significant deficiencies and
material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal control over
financial reporting which are reasonably likely to adversely affect the
registrant&#8217;s ability to record, process, summarize and report financial
information; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(b)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Any fraud, whether or not
material, that involves management or other employees who have a significant role
in the registrant&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:115%;">I, Don E. Wallette, Jr., certify that:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">1.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

report on Form 10-Q of ConocoPhillips;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a

to the period covered by this report;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">4.</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">The registrant&#8217;s other certifying

13a&#8209;15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:99.0pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(a)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">Designed such disclosure controls
and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be

the registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to us by
others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(c)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(a)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.7in;text-indent:-.35in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">(b)</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;

material, that involves management or other employees who have a significant

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:normal;">In

knowledge:</font></p>

complies with the requirements of Sections 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities
Exchange Act of 1934; and</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.5pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></p>

The fair value was estimated based on an internal discounted cash flow model using estimates of future production, an outlook of future prices using a combination of exchanges (short-term) and external pricing services companies (long-term), future operating costs and capital expenditures, and a discount rate believed to be consistent with those used by principal market participants.<span></span>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Net quantities of an enterprise's interests in proved developed reserves of either crude oil (including condensate and natural gas liquids), natural gas, synthetic oil and gas, or other nonrenewable natural resource that is intended to be upgraded into synthetic oil and gas as of the beginning and the end of the year. "Net" quantities of reserves include those relating to the enterprise's operating and nonoperating interests in properties. Quantities of reserves relating to royalty interests owned are included in "net" quantities if the necessary information is available to the enterprise. "Net" quantities does not include reserves relating to interests of others in properties owned by the enterprise. The unit of measure for reserve quantities is defined as "barrels" for oil and synthetic oil reserves or "cubic feet" or "cubic meters" for natural gas and synthetic gas reserves.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for supplemental cash flow activities, including cash, noncash, and part noncash transactions, for the period. Noncash is defined as information about all investing and financing activities of an enterprise during a period that affect recognized assets or liabilities but that do not result in cash receipts or cash payments in the period. "Part noncash" refers to that portion of the transaction not resulting in cash receipts or cash payments in the period.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for reporting segments including data and tables. Reportable segments include those that meet any of the following quantitative thresholds a) it's reported revenue, including sales to external customers and intersegment sales or transfers is 10 percent or more of the combined revenue, internal and external, of all operating segments b) the absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10 percent or more of the greater, in absolute amount of 1) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss or 2) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that did report a loss c) its assets are 10 percent or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>This item represents an other than temporary decline in value that has been recognized against an investment accounted for under the cost and equity method of accounting. The excess of the carrying amount over the fair value of the investment represents the amount of the write down which is or was reflected in earnings. The written down value is a new cost basis with the adjusted value of the investment becoming its new carrying value. Evidence of a loss in value might include, but would not necessarily be limited to, absence of an ability to recover the carrying amount of the investment or inability of the investee to sustain an earnings capacity which would justify the carrying amount of the investment.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExplorationExpense">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

<div style="display: none;">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_NumberOfOperatingSegments">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Number of operating segments. An operating segment is a component of an enterprise: (a) that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses (including revenues and expenses relating to transactions with other components of the same enterprise), (b) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the enterprise's chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance, and (c) for which discrete financial information is available. An operating segment may engage in business activities for which it has yet to earn revenues, for example, start-up operations may be operating segments before earning revenues.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExplorationExpense">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

style="display:inline-block;width:2.14px">&#160;</div>brokers for receivables arising from daily </div><div id="a8205" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:241.5px;">margin cash calls, as well as for cash deposited to meet<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.06px">&#160;</div>initial margin requirements.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.24px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a8207" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:257.5px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8208" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:273.6px;">Our trade receivables result primarily<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>from our petroleum operations and reflect a broad<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>national and </div><div id="a8210" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:289.8px;">international customer base, which limits our<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.16px">&#160;</div>exposure to concentrations of credit risk.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.62px">&#160;</div>The majority of these </div><div id="a8211" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:305.8px;">receivables have payment terms of </div><div id="a8211_34_7" </div><div id="a8211_41_59" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:245.848px;top:305.8px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>or less, and we continually monitor this exposure<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.02px">&#160;</div>and the </div><div id="a8214" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:322px;">creditworthiness of the counterparties.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.77px">&#160;</div>We do not generally require collateral to limit the exposure to loss; </div><div id="a8216" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:338.1px;">however, we will sometimes use letters of credit, prepayments<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>and master netting arrangements to mitigate </div><div id="a8217" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:354.1px;">credit risk with counterparties that both buy from<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.01px">&#160;</div>and sell to us, as these agreements permit<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.01px">&#160;</div>the amounts owed </div><div id="a8219" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:370.3px;">by us or owed to others to be offset against amounts<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>due to us. </div><div id="a8221" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:386.3px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8222" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:402.5px;">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative
</div><div id="a8223" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:418.6px;">exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts
</div><div id="a8225" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:434.6px;">with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts
</div><div id="a8226" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:450.8px;">typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert
</div></div><div id="TextBlockContainer2606" style="position:relative;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:14.08px;color:#000000;line-height:normal;width:641px;height:146px;display:inline-block;border:inherit;margin-left:-2px;margin-right:-2px;"><div id="a8231" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:0px;">to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also

</div><div id="a8241_88_10" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:510.035px;top:80.5px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>million, </div><div id="a8252" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:96.5px;">respectively.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7.61px">&#160;</div>For these instruments, </div><div id="a8252_38_2" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:210.454px;top:96.5px;">no

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for equity method investments and joint ventures. Equity method investments are investments that give the investor the ability to exercise significant influence over the operating and financial policies of an investee. Joint ventures are entities owned and operated by a small group of businesses as a separate and specific business or project for the mutual benefit of the members of the group.</p></div>

</div><div id="a2170_10_84" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:72.053px;top:32.3px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3.52px">&#160;</div>the provisions of FASB ASU No. 2016-13, &#8220;Measurement of Credit Losses<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.15px">&#160;</div>on Financial </div><div id="a2174" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:48.3px;">Instruments,&#8221; (ASC Topic 326) and its amendments, </div><div id="a2174_50_9" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:303.093px;top:48.3px;">beginning

</div><div id="a2174_75_30" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:451.734px;top:48.3px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.88px">&#160;</div>This ASU, as amended, sets </div><div id="a2175" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:64.5px;">forth the current expected credit loss model,<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.14px">&#160;</div>a new forward-looking impairment model<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.11px">&#160;</div>for certain financial </div><div id="a2179" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:80.5px;">instruments measured at amortized cost basis<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>based on expected losses rather than incurred losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5.64px">&#160;</div>This ASU, </div><div id="a2181" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:96.7px;">as amended, which primarily applies to our accounts<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.03px">&#160;</div>receivable, also requires credit losses related<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.98px">&#160;</div>to available-</div><div id="a2183" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:112.8px;">for-sale debt securities to be recorded through an allowance<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.98px">&#160;</div>for credit losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.53px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a2183_81_29" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:441.808px;top:112.8px;">The adoption of this ASU did
</div><div id="a2187" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:128.8px;">not have a material impact to our financial statements.
</div><div id="a2187_55_57" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:308.374px;top:128.8px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7.04px">&#160;</div>The majority of our receivables are due within<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.13px">&#160;</div>30 days </div><div id="a2188" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:145px;">or less.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.83px">&#160;</div>We monitor the credit quality of our counterparties through review of collections,<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>credit ratings, and </div><div id="a2190" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:161.1px;">other analyses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.57px">&#160;</div>We develop our estimated allowance for credit losses primarily using an aging method<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.97px">&#160;</div>and </div><div id="a2191" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:177.1px;">analyses of historical loss rates as well as consideration<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.9px">&#160;</div>of current and future conditions that could impact<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.98px">&#160;</div>our </div><div id="a2193" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:193.3px;">counterparties&#8217; credit quality and liquidity.</div></div><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount, excluding tax collected from customer, of revenue from satisfaction of performance obligation by transferring promised good or service to customer. Tax collected from customer is tax assessed by governmental authority that is both imposed on and concurrent with specific revenue-producing transaction, including, but not limited to, sales, use, value added and excise.</p></div>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

Excludes disclosures about product warranties.</p></div>

      id="ID_1408">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also permit us to post letters of credit as collateral, such as transactions administered through the New York Mercantile Exchange.</us-gaap:CreditDerivativeRecourseProvisions>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for condensed financial information, including the financial position, cash flows, and the results of operations of the registrant (parent company) as of the same dates or for the same periods for which audited consolidated financial statements are being presented. Alternatively, the details of this disclosure can be reported by the specific parent company taxonomy elements, indicating the appropriate date and period contexts in an instance document.</p></div>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock', window );">Fair Value Measurement</a></td>
<td class="text"><div id="TextBlockContainer2608" style="position:relative;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:14.08px;color:#000000;line-height:normal;width:634px;height:273px;display:inline-block;border:inherit;margin-left:-2px;margin-right:-2px;"><div id="a8281" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;left:4.693px;top:0px;">Note 14&#8212;Fair Value Measurement </div><div id="a8285" style="position:absolute;font-weight:bold;left:4.693px;top:16.2px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8286" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:32.4px;">We carry a portion of our assets and liabilities at fair value measured at the reporting date<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.95px">&#160;</div>using an exit price </div><div id="a8293" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:48.4px;">(i.e., the price that would be received to sell an asset<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.09px">&#160;</div>or paid to transfer a liability) and disclosed<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.13px">&#160;</div>according to </div><div id="a8295" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:64.5px;">the quality of valuation inputs under the following<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.1px">&#160;</div>hierarchy: </div><div id="a8297" style="position:absolute;font-size:16px;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:80.7px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8298" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:28.693px;top:100px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a8299" style="position:absolute;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;left:35.093px;top:99.9px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8300" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:52.688px;top:100px;">Level 1: Quoted prices (unadjusted) in an active<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.18px">&#160;</div>market for identical assets or liabilities. </div><div id="a8302" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:28.693px;top:119.6px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a8303" style="position:absolute;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;left:35.093px;top:119.4px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8304" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:52.688px;top:119.6px;">Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices that<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.17px">&#160;</div>are directly or indirectly observable. </div><div id="a8308" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:28.693px;top:139.1px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a8309" style="position:absolute;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;left:35.093px;top:138.9px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8310" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:52.688px;top:139.1px;">Level 3: Unobservable inputs that are significant<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>to the fair value of assets or liabilities. </div><div id="a8312" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:28.693px;top:157.6px;">&#160;</div><div id="a8313" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:176px;">The classification hierarchy of an asset or liability<div style="display:inline-block;width:1.95px">&#160;</div>is based on the lowest level of input significant<div style="display:inline-block;width:2.08px">&#160;</div>to its fair </div><div id="a8317" style="position:absolute;font-weight:normal;left:4.693px;top:192.2px;">value.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6.95px">&#160;</div>Those that are initially classified as <tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for the fair value of financial instruments (as defined), including financial assets and financial liabilities (collectively, as defined), and the measurements of those instruments as well as disclosures related to the fair value of non-financial assets and liabilities. Such disclosures about the financial instruments, assets, and liabilities would include: (1) the fair value of the required items together with their carrying amounts (as appropriate); (2) for items for which it is not practicable to estimate fair value, disclosure would include: (a) information pertinent to estimating fair value (including, carrying amount, effective interest rate, and maturity, and (b) the reasons why it is not practicable to estimate fair value; (3) significant concentrations of credit risk including: (a) information about the activity, region, or economic characteristics identifying a concentration, (b) the maximum amount of loss the entity is exposed to based on the gross fair value of the related item, (c) policy for requiring collateral or other security and information as to accessing such collateral or security, and (d) the nature and brief description of such collateral or security; (4) quantitative information about market risks and how such risks are managed; (5) for items measured on both a recurring and nonrecurring basis information regarding the inputs used to develop the fair value measurement; and (6) for items presented in the financial statement for which fair value measurement is elected: (a) information necessary to understand the reasons for the election, (b) discussion of the effect of fair value changes on earnings, (c) a description of [similar groups] items for which the election is made and the relation thereof to the balance sheet, the aggregate carrying value of items included in the balance sheet that are not eligible for the election; (7) all other required (as defined) and desired information.</p></div>

<td class="text">Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert to zero if we fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many also permit us to post letters of credit as collateral, such as transactions administered through the New York Mercantile Exchange.<span></span>
